To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNAJB6 gene, which encodes a chaperone protein that is expressed in skeletal muscle, was identified as the causative gene of a dominantly inherited LGMD that presents with muscle weakness and vacuoles in the skeletal muscle.

1) the exome sequencing of a family with a dominant form of LGMD and vacuoles in the skeletal muscle revealed a heterozygous missense mutation (R55Q) in the DNAJB6 gene; 2) this mutation segregated with the phenotype in the family; and 3) the R55Q mutation was associated with a decrease in protein stability and an increase in protein aggregation.
the DNAJB6 gene was identified as a novel causative gene of a dominantly‐inherited LGMD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the detection of mutations and polymorphisms in the human genome.
the identification of the genetic causes for the most prevalent types of inherited myopathies, including LGMD, congenital myopathy, and nemaline myopathy.
the study of the mechanisms that control the expression of the genes that are responsible for the production of muscle proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most common cause of the disease is an autosomal recessive mutation in the gene for myophosphorylase, which is a glycogen‐metabolizing enzyme.

the use of the word “myopathy” is acceptable for the clinical condition of muscle weakness, regardless of etiology, and the use of the term myopathy is acceptable for the pathologic condition of muscle weakness regardless of etiology.
the use of the term “muscular dystrophy” is appropriate for a group of genetic conditions that share common features of progressive muscle degeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of exome sequencing in the diagnosis of patients with neuromuscular disorders is an efficient and cost‐effective method for identifying novel disease genes and for providing accurate diagnoses.

the exome sequencing of the family revealed a heterozygous missense mutation in the DnaJ heat shock protein family (Hsp40) member B6 (DNAJB6) in all affected family members, but not in any unaffected family members.
the exome is the best way to identify the causative mutation in a patient with an unknown genetic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a new gene that is involved in the pathogenesis of a new form of LGMD, which is a group of muscle diseases with a very heterogeneous clinical and genetic spectrum.
the genetic basis of LGMD is much more complex than previously appreciated.
we can use a combination of exome sequencing and functional analysis to identify the genetic basis of an inherited disease, in this case a muscular disorder.
